facts.raw_span: erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions located on the face, chest, abdomen, and limbs
Mycological culture yielded growth of Trichophyton mentagrophytes
Images showing inflammatory lesions on the abdomen and forearm of the patient

Images showing inflammatory lesions on the abdomen and forearm of the patient

concepts.why: The patient has erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions and mycological culture yielded growth of Trichophyton mentagrophytes, which is a common cause of dermatophytosis.
The patient has a high IgE level and frequent contact with stray cats, which could trigger a hypersensitivity reaction.
The patient has eosinophilia and erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions, which are characteristic of eosinophilic dermatitis.
The patient has skin lesions and frequent contact with stray cats, which could cause contact dermatitis.

rationales.F04: Erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions are characteristic of dermatophytosis and other skin conditions.
rationales.F05: Frequent contact with stray cats may suggest a zoonotic infection, but it is not specific to any of the listed conditions.
rationales.F09: Elevated eosinophil count is more commonly associated with hypersensitivity reactions and eosinophilic dermatitis.
rationales.F10: High IgE level is more commonly associated with hypersensitivity reactions and eosinophilic dermatitis.
rationales.F11: Mycological culture yielding Trichophyton mentagrophytes is diagnostic of dermatophytosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: Mycological culture yielded growth of Trichophyton mentagrophytes, which directly supports Dermatophytosis
